themes_detail.label: Street noise surge this week
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 36 THIS WEEK, up 289% from the 9.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.3), signaling a sudden deterioration in public space conditions that warrants immediate investigation into source and timing.
evidence: 36 noise/street-sidewalk complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.2 weekly average (z-score: 7.3)
289% spike represents most recent 311 anomaly in dataset
Residential noise also elevated at 1,511 complaints over 90 days, suggesting broader noise problem
reporting_angles: What triggered the sudden surge in street noise this week? Construction, events, enforcement changes?
Interview residents in highest-complaint blocks (near Barclays Center, commercial strips) about specific noise sources

themes_detail.label: Graffiti explosion last week
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 22 LAST WEEK, up 738% from the 2.6 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 8.47), indicating either a coordinated vandalism campaign or breakdown in maintenance response across the district.
evidence: 22 graffiti complaints last week vs. 2.6 weekly average (z-score: 8.47)
738% spike tied for second-highest z-score in dataset
Typical baseline suggests 2-3 complaints weekly; 22 represents 8-9x normal volume
reporting_angles: Is this targeted vandalism or general deterioration? Map complaint locations to identify patterns.
Interview NYPD/SanDep about response times and any known crews or incidents from past 10 days

themes_detail.label: Street light outages concentrated
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints reached 18 THREE WEEKS AGO, up 251% from the 5.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.38), pointing to a specific infrastructure failure event or maintenance gap affecting public safety and darkness-related crime.
evidence: 18 street light complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 5.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.38)
Unlit streets correlate with safety concerns; recent violent incident near Barclays Center (April 5) suggests environment context
reporting_angles: Which blocks/avenues lost lighting? Cross-reference with recent DOE outages or ConEd incidents.
Has lighting been restored? If not, what's the timeline for repairs and what's causing the delay?

themes_detail.label: Elevator failures in buildings
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 21 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO, up 162% from the 8.0 weekly average (z-score: 5.67), suggesting either a specific precipitant (building code change, extreme weather) or rising maintenance failures in the aging multi-unit housing stock.
evidence: 21 elevator complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 8.0 weekly average (z-score: 5.67)
Spike coincides with broader housing quality issues: 624 plumbing complaints, 452 water leak complaints over 90 days
Elderly residents disproportionately affected; CB repeatedly requests senior center upgrades, suggesting aging population
reporting_angles: Are elevator failures concentrated in rent-stabilized or public housing? Interview residents stuck in buildings.
Has DOB increased inspections? Are landlords facing violations for non-compliance?

themes_detail.label: Food poisoning cluster alert
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints spiked to 4 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO, up 967% from the 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.21), potentially signaling a foodborne illness cluster in restaurants or food service venues that requires health department investigation.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.21)
967% spike is highest percentage increase in dataset
Baseline of 0.4 complaints/week means this represents a true anomaly, not normal variation
reporting_angles: DOHMH should confirm whether these 4 cases are linked and from which establishments. Any active outbreak investigation?
Interview affected residents about timing, symptoms, and which restaurants/vendors they visited
